rules.statement: APIs that select a hash algorithm take System.Security.Cryptography.HashAlgorithmName, not a library-defined enum of algorithms.
rules.why: HashAlgorithmName is the framework's open vocabulary, already used by RSA, ECDsa and PBKDF2. A closed enum needs a library change for every new algorithm such as SHA-384 or SHA-3.
rules.check: Look for new or changed enums listing hash algorithms (Sha1, Sha256, ...) or switch statements over them used to pick a hash.

rules.statement: Compute a digest for an arbitrary HashAlgorithmName with CryptographicOperations.TryHashData (or HashData), and take the digest length from the framework rather than hard-coding it or encoding it in an enum value.
rules.why: This way every algorithm the framework implements works without a library change, and the digest length cannot drift.
rules.check: Look for a switch from algorithm to SHA256.HashData and similar calls, hard-coded digest sizes tied to algorithm choices, or enum ordinals used as byte lengths.

rules.statement: Let the framework's CryptographicException reject an unknown hash algorithm name instead of mapping it to a fallback algorithm or a custom exception.
rules.why: The ADR says an unknown name is rejected by the framework's exception, and a deployment that needs an algorithm the framework lacks replaces the service.
rules.check: Look for default branches that silently fall back to an algorithm, or code that catches and replaces the exception when the algorithm name is unsupported.

rules.statement: Model an open set of interchangeable implementations, such as binary-to-text encodings, as a string name plus a strategy interface registered in DI with TryAddEnumerable, not as an enum dispatched through a switch.
rules.why: Packages can then add members (for example Base32) by registering another strategy, and a name is something a setting or a stored record can carry.
rules.check: Look for new enums with switch-based dispatch over an extensible set, or built-in strategies registered with AddSingleton/AddTransient instead of TryAddEnumerable.

rules.statement: A service that resolves named strategies builds its name-to-strategy map once, at construction. It compares names ordinally, fails on a duplicate name, and rejects an unregistered name with an ArgumentException that includes the name.
rules.why: Resolving through the registered collection keeps one place that validates the set, and a duplicate or unknown name fails clearly.
rules.check: Look for per-call scans of the strategy collection, case-insensitive or culture-sensitive name comparison, duplicates silently overwritten (dictionary indexer assignment), or unknown-name errors that do not include the name.

rules.statement: When an API's selection type changes (for example an enum replaced by a name), keep the hashed or encoded output of every existing call site byte-identical, or provide a migration for stored values.
rules.why: Persisted values such as grant keys and subject identifiers depend on that output, and the ADR keeps it unchanged so that no migration is needed.
rules.check: Look for a refactor that changes the default algorithm, the encoding, or the padding at an existing call site that produces persisted values.
